# Batch claim-assessment response contract correction

**Classification:** local correctness/reliability correction. **Scope:** the existing application claim-assessment boundary; no model default, provider, scientific label, scoring threshold, or safety precedence changed.

The [frozen Space Bunny screen](m12-space-bunny-scientific-result-2026-09-27.md) failed when trial 2 returned `verdests` rather than the required `verdicts`. In JSON-object compatibility mode, the shared parser prunes that unknown key and backfills the missing required array with `[]`. The application batch schema accepted that empty array and treated the malformed response as successful; all four claims then used deterministic fallback. The batch assessor is called only with one or more claims, so a successful empty verdict list cannot satisfy its prompt contract.

The red behavioral test at the real `assess_claims_batch`/LLM request boundary expected a valid second response to be used after the typo. Before the fix, only one physical call occurred and the test failed. The smallest correction adds `minItems: 1` to the `verdicts` array in `app/app/claim_verifier_batch.py`. It makes the existing schema validator reject the empty backfill, which invokes the existing bounded validation-feedback retry. There is no special case for Space Bunny or the misspelling.

After the change, the two focused batch modules' 17 tests pass. They cover a typo followed by a valid model-primary verdict in two physical calls, three malformed attempts followed by deterministic fallback, an explicit empty array, and the existing single-call per-index fallback for a valid sparse array. The retry test also asserts both requests remain on the exact Space Bunny/Stealth route with fallbacks disabled and zero prompt/completion/request price ceilings. The new regression cases live in `app/tests/test_claim_verifier_batch_schema_retry.py`; the original module remains 492 lines, below the 500-line project gate. The file-length check and targeted Ruff check/format, scoped mypy and `git diff --check` pass. Tests are offline with mocked transport; there was no provider inference or deployment in this item.

The old trial remains failed. A new comparison needs the correction released, a new preregistered protocol, and a batch probe whose previous one-physical-call cap is raised only enough to observe this existing three-attempt retry. Correct final labels and quotes without deterministic fallback remain the gate; repeated malformed replies do not qualify a model.
